desc:
The Fibonacci numbers are 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ... (each one is the sum of the previous two). Given a positive integer k, return the minimum number of Fibonacci numbers whose sum is exactly k. The same Fibonacci number may be used several times.

k = 7  -> 2   (5 + 2)
k = 10 -> 2   (8 + 2)
k = 19 -> 3   (13 + 5 + 1)
hints: Think of the Fibonacci numbers as the coin denominations of a coin-change problem. k is far too large for a dynamic program over amounts.
Only about 45 Fibonacci numbers are below 2<sup>31</sup>. Try always taking the largest coin that still fits.
Generate the Fibonacci numbers up to k and subtract the largest one not exceeding the remaining value, repeatedly, counting the subtractions.
editorial: Greedy is correct for this particular coin system. Let F be the largest Fibonacci number not above k. Some optimal answer uses F: any set of Fibonacci numbers summing to k that avoids F consists of smaller ones, and one can repeatedly merge two equal or consecutive Fibonacci numbers into the next one (F(i) + F(i-1) = F(i+1) and 2 F(i) = F(i+1) + F(i-2)) without increasing the count, until the largest term appears.

So subtract the largest Fibonacci number from k, count one, and repeat with the remainder. The remainder is smaller than the previous Fibonacci number, so each Fibonacci number is taken at most once and the loop does about 45 steps.
